Not sure why they left it out, but they forgot "-p" for "cp". It carries over the permissions of the original file to the new one. I have to use it quite often. I'm sure there's probably other stuff missing too, but I haven't really checked. I wouldn't recommend using this as a bible cheatsheet. Instead, use it more as a way to learn new commands and then check the proper documentation on them.

Edit: Ugh. They don't even have "ll". It's an alias for "ls -l". Not all linux systems have it, but most I've used do. There aren't even useful examples like "du -sh * | sort -h", "... | xargs -I {} <command> <switches> {}", or " updatedb && locate <file>". Not to mention the fact that it has a switch with question marks as its explanation under "grep". This is a cheatsheet for kangaroos.

"less is opposite of more"

I'm done with this sheet. This is ridiculous. "less" is not the opposite, but instead the enhanced version, hence their slogan "less is more".

May I introduce another "Bash command"? Its name is type, and it can tell you whether a command is a Bash builtin or external program.

$ help type
type: type [-afptP] name [name ...]
 Display information about command type.

 For each NAME, indicate how it would be interpreted if used as a
 command name.

 Options:
 -a display all locations containing an executable named NAME;
 includes aliases, builtins, and functions, if and only if
 the `-p' option is not also used
 -f suppress shell function lookup
 -P force a PATH search for each NAME, even if it is an alias,
 builtin, or function, and returns the name of the disk file
 that would be executed
 -p returns either the name of the disk file that would be executed,
 or nothing if `type -t NAME' would not return `file'.
 -t output a single word which is one of `alias', `keyword',
 `function', `builtin', `file' or `', if NAME is an alias, shell
 reserved word, shell function, shell builtin, disk file, or not
 found, respectively

 Arguments:
 NAME Command name to be interpreted.

 Exit Status:
 Returns success if all of the NAMEs are found; fails if any are not found.
